items.title: 'You're going to run the strait': The financial incentive for braving Iran's blockade
items.description: Iran is running one of the world's most critical shipping lanes as a "toll booth" and has likely made hundreds of millions of dollars of extra income from selling its own oil since the US and Israel waged war against the regime.

items.title: 'Don't say anything about the girl': Father's grim warning after child's death
items.description: Hassan Ali Al Jabal's family were all injured in an Israeli airstrike on their home in Lebanon. He does not know how to tell them one of his daughters is dead.

items.title: Live: Yemen's Houthis launch first missiles on Israel as Middle East war intensifies
items.description: Iranian-backed Houthi rebels claim responsibility for a missile attack on Israel as the war in the Middle East hits the one-month mark. Follow live.

items.title: We asked how fuel prices are affecting you — this is what you told us
items.description: From crop farmers to wildlife rescuers, here are some of the stories ABC readers told us about how the fuel crisis is impacting them.

items.title: 'It's a nightmare': Complaints pile up over Booking.com grievances
items.description: Hundreds of complaints against Booking.com are piling up as customers and hosts allege they've lost money, their property has been trashed and no one is taking responsibility.

items.title: Mal Leyland is slowly losing his memory. But there's someone he'll never forget
items.description: Adventurer and filmmaker Mal Leyland, of Ask the Leyland Brothers fame, shares his private health battle. But the TV legend is determined to retrace the cross-country trip that made him famous 60 years ago.

items.title: The unexpected type of man more women want to date
items.description: For the first time, more men than women are "marrying up" the education ladder, toppling a millennia-old tradition, an exclusive ABC analysis has revealed.

items.title: Is Labor trusting big tech too much?
items.description: As an artificial intelligence revolution approaches, the government is responding to a huge opportunity in data-centre development while balancing copyright concerns and workforce anxiety.

items.title: Will living in an apartment harm our child? My family decided to find out
items.description: In a quest for an affordable mortgage in our location of choice, my family decide to rent an apartment as a trial. Will high-rise living be a realistic alternative to a house as a place to bring up our child?

items.title: Australia has to attack misinformation about climate change, Senate report says
items.description: Australia needs to increase its efforts to fight back against misinformation about climate change, a Senate report says.

items.title: Cyclone Narelle devastates WA tourist town, airport 'obliterated'
items.description: The northern WA tourist town of Exmouth has been left isolated and heavily damaged after Cyclone Narelle tore through the town.

items.title: 'This cash cow is going to die': Why Chinese student numbers are falling
items.description: Chinese students continue to provide the lion's hare of revenue for Australian universities. But experts warn that could soon change.

items.title: Is this 'one stop shop' the way forward for Thriving Kids?
items.description: While serious workforce questions surround the new Thriving Kids scheme, the organisers of an existing program in Victoria believe its model could be scaled up.

items.title: Public transport to be free for Victorians in April
items.description: The Victorian government says public transport will be free across the state in April in a bid to relieve cost-of-living pressure as fuel prices continue to climb.

items.title: Obongjayar is the genre-defying Nigerian star challenging stereotypes
items.description: The Nigerian-British musician brightens up dark times, whether it's his adventurous solo music or scene-stealing collabs with Fred again.. and Little Simz.

items.title: Consider yourself a trivia nut? Have a crack at this quiz
items.description: We know you've come here looking for trivia glory but you're unlikely to find any today.

items.title: Many Asians try to hide cultural clothing – now it's centre stage at an exhibition
items.description: For many South Asians, museums in the West have historically been places where their cultures were displayed as static artefacts. An exhibition like The Offbeat Sari has flipped that script, presenting South Asian creativity as innovative and globally influential.

items.title: Farmers face 'decision paralysis' as fuel costs threaten viability
items.description: The sudden rise in fuel costs is forcing farmers to make difficult decisions, such as laying off workers and selling equipment to keep their businesses running.

items.title: Former AFL footballer asked how much he drank before he was allegedly raped
items.description: Daniel Hayes was 17 years old when he was allegedly raped by his coach while playing in an Australian Rules football talent league in Victoria.

items.title: Darwin's ambulance service fails overnight as 61 Triple Zero calls abandoned
items.description: Darwin's ambulance service has reached a "critical failure point" as 42 per cent of Triple Zero calls were abandoned overnight.

items.title: Cowboys score three tries in eight minutes to complete comeback against Storm
items.description: The Cowboys completed a second half comeback, scoring three tries in eight minutes, to defeat the Storm 28-24.

items.title: 'Not acceptable': Xerri facing ban after rubbing blood on Dons skipper's face
items.description: North Melbourne survives a nervy finish to break a decade-long drought against Essendon as star ruckman Tristan Xerri rubs blood on Andrew McGrath's face in a heated exchange.

items.title: Why some states will get an extra hour of sleep on Easter Sunday
items.description: Most states and territories are preparing to turn back clocks for the end of daylight saving this week. Here's what you need to know.

items.title: Gout beaten by Kennedy in epic Maurie Plant re-match as history repeats
items.description: In an identical performance to their titanic battle 12 months ago, Lachlan Kennedy edges out Gout Gout to win the men's 200 metres at the Maurie Plant Meet in Melbourne.

items.title: Senegal shows off contested AFCON trophy as legal battle rages
items.description: Senegal defies the decision to strip it of the Africa Cup of Nations trophy by parading it around the pitch before a 2-0 victory over Peru at the Stade de France in Paris.
